newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges fall, traders seen pricing down.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges fall, traders seen pricing down.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges fetched lower numbers early on Friday as some traders eyeing cargoes were said to be trying to push the market down.

High sulphur barges exchanged hands in the early morning at $79 and $79.50 a tonne fob ARA before moving up to the $81 region, which is 50 cents below Thursday's closing level. Traders put the total traded at 10 kT.
"The market started at the low numbers as some traders are pricing cargoes and tried to push the market down," one trader said.
One of the parties to the lowest deal was said to be a trading house that actively tried to drive the market lower earlier this week against a major's bids to send prices to the upside.
Bunkers were heard done at $83/$84, or some $1 below trades a day earlier, for 380 CST material, traders said.
Low sulphur barges were actively talked this morning but no trades were reported with sellers still insisting on $96, or last done this week, while some buyers moved $2 further down to about $91.
"I had enquiries this morning for 1,000 tonnes and 5,000 tonnes this month. I can do may be 1,000 or 2,000 tonnes," one seller said.
"Several people are interested in buying for this month. One offer came in at $91 but I was not even prepared to discuss that number. I want to see $96," the seller added.
